D004-D017_h001.question_both:
It’s hard to put into words without sounding crazy, but it’s been going on maybe a few months now, on and off. I do a lot of surveillance at night, stakeouts, that kind of thing, and lately I can’t shake this feeling that something terrible is about to happen, like everything is winding down. Not just a bad week—more like the world is thinning out, hollowing. I’ll be sitting in my car watching a building and it feels like it’s all about to collapse, or like none of this is actually going to be here much longer.

At the same time I’ve gotten really fixated on how I look. I catch my reflection in a shop window between jobs and I’m convinced there’s something off—my face looks distorted, like my jaw’s caved in a bit or my skin’s…wrong somehow. Photos make it worse; I can barely stand to look at them because I’m sure I see some defect other people either don’t notice or won’t admit to. I ask my ex or a client in a roundabout way if I look different, and they brush it off, but it doesn’t really convince me.
D004-D017_h001.question_a:
I’ve been like this for about a year now. I still work—follow cheating spouses, do background checks, sit in my car for hours—but it all feels pointless because I’m convinced it’s not going to matter much longer.

It’s not just a vague “things are bad” feeling. I’m certain something big and catastrophic is coming, like the world’s about to collapse in on itself. I’ll be tailing someone, watching them walk their dog, and I catch myself thinking, “They have no idea none of this will exist soon.” It feels less like an opinion and more like I already know the ending to a movie.

I also can’t shake the idea that something is fundamentally wrong with my body—like my insides are decaying or my face is subtly deforming, even though doctors and my ex say I look fine. I’ll check in the mirror, prod at my skin a bit, but it’s not like I’m spending hours grooming or doing rituals. Mostly I just accept it as another sign everything is breaking down.

I make it to jobs, pay bills, talk to clients, but all of that is filtered through this certainty that we’re on borrowed time.
D004-D017_h001.question_b:
I spend most of my days tailing other people for a living, but lately I can’t even stand to look at myself. For at least the past year, I’ve been convinced there’s something horribly wrong with my face—like my nose is twisted and huge, my skin is pitted and deformed. In the mirror it looks monstrous, like something you’d see after an explosion. I know my ex and my coworkers say they don’t see it, but I’m sure they’re lying or just don’t want to scare me.

It’s gotten to where I can’t leave the apartment without spending an hour or more in the bathroom, rechecking the mirror from different angles, picking at my skin, trying to even things out, shaving and reshaving. I’ll change shirts three or four times because I think certain colors make my face look worse. If I catch my reflection in a car window on a stakeout, I lose the thread of what I’m doing and start fixing my hair or adjusting my collar over and over.

Sometimes it feels like my face is so ruined that it’s a sign the world’s falling apart—that everything’s deteriorating, not just me. I keep thinking we’re all headed toward some sort of collapse, and my face is proof something terrible is coming.

I keep feeling like there’s something wrong under my skin—like a deformity or some kind of growth that everyone can see but no one will say straight out. I’ve checked in the mirror, even taken a few photos on my phone, but it’s hard to tell anything for sure. Doctors say everything looks “normal,” but that doesn’t line up with how people act around me. It’s like everyday comments and looks are all secretly about this thing that’s wrong with me.

I’ll walk into a hardware store and hear two guys talking about “that rotting one” or “something crawling under there,” and I know they mean my face. On TV, if there’s a line about someone “infested” or “falling apart,” it feels like it’s directed at me. It can’t be a coincidence the wording lines up with what I feel.

I’m sure there’s something seriously wrong under my skin, like the chemicals I’ve used at work got into my face and are eating it from the inside. Doctors keep telling me I’m fine, but I can feel it. I check mirrors, sure, but I’m not standing there for hours or doing weird rituals or anything like that. I still do my pest control routes, drive, pay bills. D004-D017_h002.question_b:

My kids and my ex-wife say they don’t notice anything, but I can’t shake the idea that they’re just being polite.

At work, if a customer glances at me or whispers to someone, I’m sure they’re talking about how messed up my face looks. Even if guys at the shop laugh about something unrelated, my first thought is, “They’re laughing at me.” I’ll replay little comments all day, trying to figure out what they really meant.

I’m in the bathroom constantly, checking different mirrors, different angles, taking pictures and zooming in, picking at my skin, trying to “fix” it.
